items.prompt: Can group behavior help animals survive?
Name one way a group helps its members.
items.answer: Defending against predators (or finding food, caring for young)

steps: Groups defend, feed, and care for young.

items.prompt: How do meerkats on guard help the group?

steps: Guards warn the group so members escape danger.

items.prompt: How does pack hunting help wolves?
items.answer: They catch large prey for more food

steps: Packs catch prey a lone wolf cannot.

items.prompt: How can more food help a group reproduce?
items.answer: Healthier animals can raise more young

items.prompt: What evidence shows group behavior helps survival?
items.answer: Grouped animals survive or reproduce more than solitary ones

steps: Comparing grouped vs solitary outcomes is evidence.

items.prompt: How do bees in a hive help each other?
items.answer: They share work like gathering food and caring for young

steps: Shared work lets the hive thrive.

items.prompt: Does group living have any costs?

steps: Groups can have competition and disease spread.

items.prompt: Name one cost of living in a group.
items.answer: Competition for food (or faster disease spread)

steps: Groups can compete and spread disease.

items.prompt: Do many animals live in groups?
Explain how taking turns on guard helps meerkats survive.
items.answer: Guards warn of predators so others can feed safely and escape danger

items.prompt: Evaluate how pack hunting helps wolves reproduce.
items.answer: More food keeps wolves healthy enough to raise young, improving reproduction

items.prompt: What would you measure to test if group behavior helps a species?
items.answer: Survival, food gathered, or number of young for groups versus solitary animals

steps: These measures compare grouped and solitary outcomes.

items.prompt: Evaluate the claim that group living has only benefits.
items.answer: It is incomplete, because groups also have costs like competition and disease

steps: Groups have both benefits and costs.

items.prompt: Why does group behavior help most when benefits outweigh costs?
items.answer: If the benefits like defense are larger than costs like competition, members do better

steps: Net benefit determines whether grouping helps.
